questions.text:
Pohutukawa Preserves is a Hawke's Bay-based producer of artisan jams and chutneys. The table above shows their cost and pricing information. Annual fixed costs are $42,000.

Calculate: (a) the contribution margin per jar, (b) the break-even point in units, and (c) the profit if 8,000 jars are sold. Show all working.
questions.markingGuide: Correct identification of variable costs, contribution margin calculation, and break-even formula application.

questions.text:
Pōhutukawa Preserves expects to sell 9,500 jars this year.

(i) Calculate the expected annual profit.
(ii) Calculate the margin of safety in units and as a percentage.
(iii) If Pōhutukawa wants a target profit of $30,000, how many jars must they sell?
questions.markingGuide: Correct treatment of variable and fixed costs in profit calculation, margin of safety, and target profit.

questions.text:
Pohutukawa is considering two distribution strategies for a new organic range. The table above shows the details of each option.

Calculate the expected profit for each option and recommend which strategy Pohutukawa should adopt. Justify your recommendation.
questions.expectedAnswer: Option A: Contribution = $16 - $8 = $8 per jar. Total contribution = 3,500 × $8 = $28,000. Profit = $28,000 - $15,000 = $13,000. Option B: Contribution = $13 - $8 = $5 per jar. Total contribution = 7,000 × $5 = $35,000. Profit = $35,000 - $15,000 = $20,000. Option B maximises profit despite the lower price, because the higher volume more than compensates.
questions.markingGuide: Show calculations for both options and explain how changes affect break-even and profit.

questions.text: Based on your CVP analysis, make a strategic recommendation to Pōhutukawa Preserves. Consider not just profit maximisation but also: brand positioning (artisan vs mass-market), risk (what if actual demand is 25% below estimates?), and long-term sustainability. Justify your recommendation.
questions.expectedAnswer: While Option B generates $7,000 more profit, other factors matter. Risk analysis: if demand drops 25%, Option A profit = (2,625 × $8) - $15,000 = $6,000; Option B profit = (5,250 × $5) - $15,000 = $11,250. Option B still wins under pessimistic scenario. However, Option A maintains artisan positioning, which may support higher long-term brand value and customer loyalty. Recommendation: Option B, because it maximises profit in both base and pessimistic scenarios, and the higher volume builds wider brand awareness. But Pōhutukawa should maintain their artisan image through premium labelling and storytelling, not just price.
questions.markingGuide: Link CVP findings to strategic business decisions with justified reasoning including risk analysis.
